 Open Navigation Menu Menu Culture Latest OTT releases (November 9-November 15): 18 new movies and TV shows on Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar and more
 Looking to add to your watchlist? Shanaya Kapoor plays a teen investigating her twin sister’s murder in Student of the Year: After Dark , and Sauron escalates his war against the Elves in the third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power By Prabal Sharma 9 November 2026 Shanaya Kapoor in Student of the Year: After Dark It’s time for your weekly update of the latest OTT releases, and the next seven days have the perfect blend of movies and TV shows to satiate all your bingeing needs. Shanaya Kapoor investigates a chilling campus murder at St. Teresa’s in the mystery thriller Student of the Year: After Dark ; Sauron escalates his war against the Elves to forge the One Ring in the third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power ; Diane Morgan returns to trace the history of film as the clueless Philomena Cunk in the mockumentary comedy Cunk on Cinema; Brad Pitt–led survival thriller Heart of the Beast and Jessica Chastain’s horror flick Other Mommy become available on demand.
 Heart of the Beast (November 10) 
 David Ayer directs this intense survival thriller starring Brad Pitt as James Belmont, a retired Special Forces officer who crashes his plane in the remote Alaskan wilderness. Stranded alongside his loyal combat dog Odin, James must navigate 58 miles of hostile terrain, fending off wolves and extreme elements while battling his own severe physical injuries. The narrative centres on the endurance required to reach civilisation and the unbreakable bond between the soldier and his canine companion.
 Available to buy & rent on BookMyShow Stream, Apple TV, Prime Video 
 Other Mommy (November 10) 
 Jessica Chastain and Jay Duplass lead this James Wan–produced horror feature directed by Rob Savage. Adapted from Josh Malerman’s novel, the plot follows a fractured family as a young girl’s seemingly imaginary friend suddenly appears. The situation rapidly escalates into a terrifying domestic nightmare when the titular entity manifests as a manipulative supernatural presence determined to replace the household’s matriarch violently.
 Available to buy & rent on Apple TV, Prime Video 
 Alicia’s Law (November 11) 
 Netflix delivers a Mexican adaptation of the hit legal drama The Good Wife , splitting the first season into two parts. Fernanda Castillo stars as Alicia, a woman forced to resurrect her dormant legal career after her Supreme Court Justice husband, played by Juan Manuel Bernal, goes to prison amid a highly public corruption and sex scandal. The series tracks her professional reemergence and the complex choices she faces in redefining her independence.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Avedon (November 11) 
 Following its premiere at the Cannes Film Festival, Ron Howard’s latest documentary chronicles the monumental cultural impact of iconic photographer Richard Avedon. Relying on archival footage and contemporary interviews with figures like Calvin Klein, Isabella Rossellini and Twiggy, the film examines how Avedon fundamentally altered visual media by blending commercial fashion with stark, confrontational portraiture.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Body (November 11) 
 Created by Quinn Shephard, this eight-episode coming-of-age psychological horror series centres on a group of rebellious Catholic school girls. When a high school dance-team initiation goes horribly wrong on Halloween night, the teenagers suddenly begin experiencing terrifying prophetic visions that quickly trigger mass hysteria throughout their small town. The ensemble cast includes Kristina Bogic, Sara Boustany, Geena Meszaros, Sofia Wylie and Nnamdi Asomugha navigating the escalating fallout of their supernatural visions.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Gospel of Christmas (November 11) 
 Tyler Perry writes and directs this holiday musical feature led by R&B powerhouses Fantasia Barrino and Durrell “Tank” Babbs. The story follows a New York pastor grappling with a profound crisis of faith during the hectic holiday season. He must somehow find the spiritual and emotional resolve to guide his family, his struggling congregation and his local neighbourhood through a series of escalating tribulations right before Christmas.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 3 (November 11) 
 Picking up five years after the devastating fall of Eregion, the third season finds Middle-earth engulfed in open war. Sauron now commands from his newly completed tower of Barad-dûr in Mordor, obsessively working to forge the One Ring to achieve total domination. With the Dwarves sealed deep within Khazad-dûm and the surviving Elves defending Lindon and Rivendell, the fractured realms of Men, Elves and Wizards must finally align their forces against the Dark Lord. The new episodes also introduce Jamie Campbell Bower to the ensemble cast as Galadriel’s long-lost love, Celeborn.
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 Allen (November 12) 
 Ludo Studio, the team behind the hit animated series Bluey , delivers its first feature-length production with this Australian science fiction comedy. T.J. Power stars as Petey, a man who has spent twenty years struggling to move on after his alien best friend disappeared during their childhood. When Petey builds a makeshift satellite and accidentally summons his friend back to Earth, their happy reunion is cut short by the discovery that the alien is hiding a massive secret that threatens the entire planet.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Christmas Switch (November 12) 
 Real-life twin actresses Felice and Happy Jankell star as sisters with wildly contrasting personalities in this Swedish holiday romantic comedy directed by Adam Pålsson. In the weeks leading up to Christmas, the siblings decide to swap lives and immerse themselves in completely new environments. The temporary arrangement forces them to confront their past choices while unexpectedly finding romance amidst the holiday chaos. The supporting cast features Christian Fandango Sundgren, Anastasios Soulis and Celie Sparre.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Empress season 3 (November 12) 
 The hit German historical drama returns for a third and final season, with Devrim Lingnau and Philip Froissant reprising their roles as the imperial couple. Following the devastating Sardinian War, Emperor Franz returns to the court as a deeply traumatised man, heavily burdened by the immense loss of his soldiers on the battlefield. The concluding episodes examine the rapid unravelling of the Habsburg monarchy as the young marriage is severely tested by the pressure to produce a male heir, escalating political tensions and a painful personal loss. The mounting crises ultimately force Elisabeth into an impossible choice between following her own heart and fulfilling her demanding duty to the people.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Never Surrender (November 12) 
 This Indonesian action thriller stars Lukman Sardi as Eyang Hari, an ageing former soldier who is attempting to live a peaceful life in a remote village alongside his two grandchildren. When a ruthless criminal syndicate from Jakarta manages to track them down, his isolated home becomes the target of a violent siege. Forced to become a one-man army, he must rely entirely on his dormant military experience and confront his own past traumas to defend his family.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Being Heumann (November 13) 
 An adaptation of Judy Heumann’s memoir into this biographical drama detailing the historic 1977 federal building sit-in. Ruth Madeley stars as Heumann, who leads a coalition of disability rights activists in a gruelling occupation to force the implementation of crucial civil rights legislation. The film tracks the escalating weeks of the protest as the group battles bureaucratic delays from the United States Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare, played by Mark Ruffalo. Dylan O’Brien co-stars as a television journalist who embeds himself with the activists to broadcast their standoff to the outside world.
 Streaming on Apple TV 
 Heartland (November 13) 
 Written and directed by Shana Feste, this American mystery thriller explores the dark underbelly of the Nashville music scene. Jessica Chastain stars as Misty Jones, a former country music megastar whose life is completely upended when her niece abruptly disappears. The narrative follows her descent into the city’s criminal element as she launches a desperate search to find her missing relative. The ensemble cast includes John Hawkes, Carter Faith, Garrett Hedlund, Jennifer Nettles and Ross Lynch.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Murder in Galicia (November 13) 
 This Spanish true crime limited series dramatises a shocking 2015 domestic violence and murder case. Tristán Ulloa and Carlos Blanco lead the cast in a narrative that begins with a brutal home invasion, leaving a woman severely injured. As she recovers in the intensive care unit, a tenacious local investigator becomes increasingly convinced her husband orchestrated the initial assault. The series tracks the escalating tension as the authorities desperately attempt to navigate bureaucratic hurdles and implement protective measures before the husband can finish what he started.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Student of the Year: After Dark (November 13) 
 Directed by Reema Maya, this web series pivots the established Bollywood franchise into a dark mystery thriller. Shanaya Kapoor makes her digital streaming debut alongside Divik Sharma as the setting returns to the elite halls of St. Teresa’s. The narrative completely abandons traditional campus romance in favour of a suspenseful murder investigation after a young woman is found dead on the school grounds. The plot explores the dangerous secrets concealed within the prestigious institution while reimagining the familiar student competition as a high-stakes survival scenario.
 Streaming on JioHotstar 
 The Third Murder (November 13) 
 A Malayalam crime thriller, The Third Murder focuses on a baffling serial killer case. After a businessman is murdered in the same manner as a local drug peddler, DYSP Christy, played by Saiju Kurup, recruits an ex-cop to assist the investigation. The trail eventually points toward a troubled teenager caught in a bitter conflict with his eccentric father, kicking off a desperate race to uncover the hidden motives and prevent another casualty.
 Streaming on ManoramaMAX 
 Cunk on Cinema (November 15) 
 Diane Morgan returns as the notoriously clueless mockumentary presenter Philomena Cunk in this three-part comedy series created by Charlie Brooker. The production traces the entire history of film, following Cunk as she explores everything from the invention of the camera to the modern implementation of artificial intelligence. The format relies heavily on her conducting completely serious, absurd interviews with a wide range of bewildered industry professionals, featuring appearances by director Michael Bay, actor Benedict Cumberbatch and screenwriter Steven E. de Souza.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Chosen season 6 (November 15) 
 Creator Dallas Jenkins helms the penultimate season of this historical drama, dedicating the new episodes entirely to the final 24 hours of Jesus’s earthly life. The narrative specifically tracks the events of Good Friday, beginning with the betrayal by Judas and culminating in the crucifixion. Jonathan Roumie reprises his starring role as Jesus of Nazareth alongside a massive returning ensemble that includes Shahar Isaac, Elizabeth Tabish, Paras Patel, Luke Dimyan, Paul Ben-Victor as King Herod and Andrew James Allen as Pontius Pilate.
 Streaming on Prime Video
